column3: the hottest field code left after the event engine, which a native-mode profile over the save movies put at about a third of all interpreted instructions. The object loop (called from the field main loop at `$C0:00D3`) moves each object slot, activates it by the screen window (`$C0:A88D`, native), and for objects in view steps the animation delay and queues the object for a new frame (`$76`/`$77`, linked through `$1081`), recomputes its 9-bit screen position (`$0A00`/`$0A80`) and moves it between the doubly linked row lists by screen Y (`$0E00`, `$0E80`/`$0E81`); the callees are call-outs, all of them native. The sprite table builder (entered by `BRL` from `$C0:00DB` as well as by `JSR`) walks the row lists from the bottom and has each object draw itself: `$C0:B701` brings its 4, 8, 12 or 24 sprite records at `$7F:4BC0` up to date (the 4-record repositioning and reload are `$C0:B788`/`$C0:B8CA`; the 8- and 12-record ones `$C0:BA65`, `$C0:BFF2`, `$C0:BCDC`, `$C0:C2BF` and the helpers clearing the object from `$0BC0`, `$C0:E9E2`-`$C0:EA1F`, stay in the original as call-outs, and the 24-record layout stops at `$C0:C73A`), then `$C0:B309` writes the high table bytes and the sprites into one of three OAM ranges by priority through the WRAM data port `$2180` with the direct page at `$2100` (its four copies, which push and pull the high table bytes, share one port), and the builder hides the entries each range used last frame beyond this frame's. `$C0:7F9A` computes each layer's tile map edge indexes with four local helpers (`$C0:813D`, `$C0:81A1`, `$C0:81D6`, `$C0:8218`, inlined with their stack bytes); `$C0:91AC` the three layers' scroll accumulators and pixel move counts; `$C0:A521` unpacks a map's tile layers and attributes at load. The graphics routines copy 32-byte sprite tiles (straight from bank `$D2`-`$D5` or `$7F`, or mirrored through `$C0:FD00` into the WRAM port) and read an object's current frame number; they are called by the frame builder `$C0:CBDC`, which stays in the original, from the frame queue `$C0:CA76`, which reads the H/V counters (`$213F`, `$2137`, `$213D`) and stops at a scanline limit like the event scheduler, so it stays interpreted too. All calls in every movie match (fair-companion: `move_object` 241948, `link`/`unlink_object_row` 68790/68758, `update_screen_position`, `draw_object_sprites` and `update_object_sprites` 57737, `position_sprites` 56331, `update_objects` 11515, `copy_sprite_tile` 17650, `read_animation_frame` 9036; `unpack_tile_maps` 4-15 per movie); every routine is reached. All pass 60000 fuzzed states on two seeds from a field state. The sprite routines need the game's ranges: the object slot `$6D` below `$80` and the record offsets `$1700-$17FF` below `$3000` (and for `$C0:B788`/`$C0:B8CA` X a slot), and `$C0:B309` its high table pointers (`$0181`/`$0185`/`$0189`) inside `$0900-$091F`; with random values the records and pointers reach I/O space past the end of bank `$7F` or bank `$00`'s RAM, where open bus and the WRAM port make both sides differ. With these, `on` mode interprets 31% fewer instructions over the 15 save movies (661 million to 453 million; from 20% to 64% fewer per movie, except `menus-epoch` and `menus-field-menu`, which stay in menus, under 3%) **Phase 3a rewrite** (RECOMP.md, "Phase 3a: the field subsystem off the machine"): `field_tick_object_animation` (was `field_step_object_animation`) and `field_read_animation_frame` are in `field/animation.c` now, `field_leave_object_row`/`field_join_object_row` (were `field_unlink_object_row`/`field_link_object_row`) in `field/object_update.c`, the objects' view in `field/object_view.c`. The update runs its steps as C (timed as those routines), and the sprite table's building its draws, where their entries' guards would take the state and the step calls nothing of the original's. Shadow totals are the predecessor's in calls, mismatches (none) and skips; interrupted calls rose where that work now runs in the caller's time: `field_update_objects` 6 to 17 of 193199, `field_build_sprite_table` 267 to 336, `field_draw_object_sprites` 837 to 1713, `field_update_object_sprites` 78 to 855. Fuzzed against the predecessor (seed 1), mismatched before and after: `field_update_objects` 0 and 0 of 2000; `field_update_object_in_window` 0 of 20000 and 0 of 10065 (the rest turned away by its guard: an odd current object); `field_leave_object_row` and `field_join_object_row` 0 of 20000 and 0 of 5707 each (odd links turned away); `field_move_object`, `_unbounded` and `field_update_screen_position` 0 of 20000 and 0 of 10065 each; `field_tick_object_animation` 0 of 20000 and 0 of 5710 (the delay entry past its bank or odd queue links turned away); `field_read_animation_frame` 0 of 20000 and 0 of 6652 (an odd object, or the facing tables past the bank, turned away); `field_build_sprite_table` 0 of 0 on both (every state runs its draws past the call-out budget); `field_draw_object_sprites` and `field_update_object_sprites` 0 of 20000 and 0 of 10017; `field_position_sprites` and `field_load_and_position_sprites` 0 of 20000 and 0 of 10248; `field_position_sprites` loose, with the records anywhere, 3452 of 19995 before and 0 of 13878 after, the records that would run past bank `$7F` turned away by the rewrite's guard; `field_compute_layer_edges` and `field_update_layer_scroll` 0 and 0 of 20000; `field_unpack_tile_maps` 0 of 2000 and 0 of 1006 (a stream that would reach the layers' page turned away); `field_copy_sprite_tile` and `_flipped` 0 and 0 of 20000. Combined pass (RECOMP.md, "Phase 3a: event onto the field's objects"): the object guards take slots inside the tables, which halves every object entry's compared states (`field_read_animation_frame` 0 of 3326, `field_tick_object_animation` 0 of 2896, `field_move_object` 0 of 5060, `field_object_in_the_way` 0 of 5009 with the object count 1 to 63, ...); `field_read_animation_frame`'s split into a finder and a taker first mismatched 517 of 3326 (a frame table where nothing answers reads the last byte on the bus, which the finder had made the animation's number rather than the table's bank; it looks the table up last again) and then 0; `field_position_sprites` and `field_load_and_position_sprites` are fuzzed with the object in X the current one (their guard's condition, the game's only case), 0 of 20000 before and after, and loose 0 of 13878 before and after. column3: the ROM side of the scenes the boot decompresses to `$7E:3000` and runs from RAM: the attract sequence and title screen (frames 0-1637 of every movie), the jet bike race, the endings, and the title again after a game over. Written as logic apart from the registers (Phase 3): the early ports that moved emulated registers about (the NMI, the sprite lists, the scaler, the multiply) were rewritten, and every entry leaves only what liveness says its callers read. The boot points the NMI and IRQ stubs at bank C3's handlers, turns the line interrupt on at line 211 where the scene's mode bits ask (the new `tm_set_line`, [PLATFORM.md](PLATFORM.md)), and decompresses the program (a call-out) from the resource table at `$FE:0003` (`scene/scene_data.h`), stopping at `$7E:3000`. The NMI's frame work inlines the controller and pause check `$C3:0A8E` and the song update `$C3:09A4`; the task lists, the pause sound and the sound driver are call-outs; it stops at the auto-joypad wait's `BNE` while the read is busy (the wait on it is the original's) and ports the L+R+Select+Start reset as far as its jump to `$00:FF00`. The sequence interpreter ([tools/disasm/seqscript.py](../tools/disasm/seqscript.py) has the command set) runs each channel's commands until one yields, with the task list helpers `$C3:0CB8`-`$C3:0CF8` inline and command `$AB`'s video register writes as service calls for the nine registers the scripts write; the carry and overflow its callers read are carried through the commands. A command no script has (a store outside low RAM, another register, a task search that never ends, a script that never yields) puts the pointer back and runs the rest of the run as a call-out to the original's loop from the entry's own `JSR` site. Shadow mode now compares a stop at the loop's head `$C3:0B03` at the right pass, but the port can't stop there yet: a command it gives up on has already written the scratch cell `$F0` and the flags (RECOMP.md, "Between the waves: the validator"; docs/TODO.md). `$C3:0C28`, where the sound wait goes on, is not an entry; it could be now, since an entry the original reaches inside a run no longer takes the run's call-outs (Call-outs, above), as a local build that registered it showed. column3: the map the mode at `$C2:0000` shows behind its sprite objects, and what its object scripts' scroll and redraw commands call out to. It is three planes of 96 x 64 map tiles of 16 x 16 pixels: a plane's map is a byte per map tile in work RAM, the byte picks one of 256 tile groups (four background tiles, two by two) also in work RAM, and the group's tiles go to a 64 x 32 tilemap in VRAM, two 32 x 32 screens side by side. Three words of bank `$C2` (`$C2:0556`, `$C2:055C`, `$C2:0562`) say where a plane's groups, map and tilemap are, through one accessor that `menu/object_script.c`'s write-a-map-byte command shares. Scrolling moves the plane's scroll shadow a tile at a time with its top-left map tile, and each uncovered tile column or row becomes 32 tilemap words built in the mode's upload buffer at `$7E:F000` and queued for the next vblank (`$C2:059D`/`$C2:0607` and `$C2:06A1`/`$C2:070B` per direction, `$C2:0811`/`$C2:08DB` to set a strip up, `$C2:0773`/`$C2:07C2` and `$C2:0843`/`$C2:088F` to build one, `$C2:090D`/`$C2:0961` to queue it, all inlined). A redraw is the same for the whole plane, eighteen blocks of sixteen map tiles (`$C2:0A6C`, `$C2:0AAE` inlined) sent straight to VRAM by `menu_map_upload_block` with the screen blanked; that routine was `menu_object_upload_sprite_tiles` in `menu/display.c`, in the early style, and moved here with the RAM cell it reads, which is the upload buffer's cursor and not a sprite tile pointer. The map's origin is two arrays of a word per plane and not one array of three words `$04` apart (RECOMP.md, "Phase 3, wave 2: the menus' map"); `$C2:2720` sets both planes' from the party's tile. A plane number that isn't 1, 2 or 3 makes the original spin at `$C2:059B`, `$C2:069F` or `$C2:0A6A`, which the three entries hand back to the interpreter with `m_stop_at_own` and an empty set. Calls over the whole movie library, none mismatching: `menu_map_scroll_y` 7460, `menu_map_scroll_x` 5128, `menu_map_upload_block` 1620 (2 interrupted), `menu_map_redraw` 90 (36 interrupted), `menu_map_centre_on_party` 23; `menus-epoch` reaches them most, and every movie but `title-start` reaches some. Fuzzed from a `menus-epoch` state with D = 0, the upload buffer's cursor kept (`--keep 7E00E0-7E00E2`), the queue's tail inside the queue (`--fill 7E005F-7E005F=00-70`) and the scroll's step small (`--fill 7E0001-7E0001=00-08`, and `F8-FF` for the other direction): 20000 states each on two seeds for the scrolls in each direction, the block upload and the map centring, 5000 for the redraw, and 5000 each of the refused plane number; none mismatching. Fuzzing found six differences no movie reaches: a 16-bit `DEC` and `INC` the draft's listing showed as 8-bit (the script pointer's step back, the wipe's count), a palette offset wrapping in 16 bits where the original's indexed store runs into bank `$7F`, the fade tables' carry (the loop's last `CPX` sets it), the preset loop's Y, which callers read, and the flags of the table dispatch's unknown targets

column3: the 19 timed slots that move the combatants (0-10) and the anchor points (11-18) along lines, jumps under gravity, spirals, orbits, homing jumps and turning chases, with the sine and arctangent tables through the multiplier. The two handler tables dispatch in C, and a type past them calls out where the original's table points. The per-slot arrays are named as arrays of 19, the anchors' elements 11-18, since the original's second table uses the same offsets from bases 11 elements on. The loop carries what the handlers leave in A (A's high byte is live after it), and the handlers are guarded on A's high byte 0, as the loop leaves it; called as entries of their own, the handlers and `battle_place_formation` declare A's low byte dead (`DC_AL`: no caller reads it) and leave it as it is. All calls over the library match (the loop 431221; the handlers 348-43353, the orbits 85342, the sine 176306, the multiply 192738; `$CF:F1F8` and `$CF:F405` aren't reached). Fuzzed 20000 states twice (two seeds) each, from a battle state; the handlers with A's high byte 0 and a combatant slot: all match, the loop 1280 and 1299 skipped where a called-out handler doesn't return. Fuzzing found the homing jump's 16-bit `INC`, the chase's order of reads and writes where a stray slot offset makes its tables overlap, and the anchors' offsets into the 19-slot arrays, which the original's indexed accesses carry into bank `$7F`. With `DC_AL`, fuzzed again from `gato-battle` at frame 20000 (`--db 7E --d 0000`, the handlers with A below `$0100` and a combatant slot): the fifteen handlers and `battle_place_formation` 20000 states on each of two seeds, all matching (three handler states skipped), and the same again with the fuzzer after the fuzz and timing pass (one state skipped)

column3: the per-frame pass that sorts the battle objects by depth and writes their sprites to the OAM buffer, the hottest non-waiting code in the fight: under each object its number sprites, marker or effect sprites, its tiles and parts, what goes over it, its shadow, and while effects run its trail of four afterimages. Rewritten in Phase 3 (out of `battle/sprites.c`): the direct page is the drawing page's and the object's cells named, and the marker's and effect sprites' cells the battle page's; the entries that take A's high byte into an index are guarded on it being 0, as a frame's drawing leaves it. All calls over the library match (409679, 1855861 each for the per-object routines and 1861677 tile copies, 3056 trails with 5816 afterimages, 246014 effect sprite sets). Fuzzed 20000 states twice (two seeds) each, from a battle state; the per-object routines with the drawing page and `battle_oam_next` below `$8000`, the whole pass with each object's part count at most 16 and each sprite set's count at most 8. With counts unbounded the sprites run on over the drawing page's own cells, and the draw list is read back from them; since the fuzzer stops a port's own loops (Fuzzing, above), those states run too, and 40 of 20000 differ, 28 of them with the port running on where the original returns (TODO.md). Fuzzing found what the original's indexing does there, all of it now in the port: the position's Y is read after the X was written (an object past the eleven reads it from the scratch), the object number, counts and cells are read back where the original reloads them, its direct-page indexes wrap in bank `$00`, the last of the eight tile groups isn't counted, and the tile copy's source can cover its own `JSR`'s return address, which the port writes. With `battle_oam_next` at `$F900` or above, the copy's destination reaches the stack and the original's own return address, which no port can follow
